families.family_description: OH-rich biopolymer/film-former hosts retain a plasticised acid-water phase to preserve proton pathways into the cold window.
descriptor_match: D2: DES/plasticiser and hydrated acid motifs support bound polar-fluid continuity at low temperature.
D3: starch/chitosan/PVA-type hosts are flexible hydrogen-bonded matrices rather than brittle inorganic frameworks.
D6: abundant OH/NH and phosphate sites create dense proton-relay networks.
D7: biopolymer hosts can retain acid/water without immediate structural disintegration.

families.family_description: Tubular or fibrous 1-D fillers confine phosphoric-acid-rich domains and guide interconnected transport channels within a soft host.
descriptor_match: D5: attapulgite and halloysite are explicitly linked to nanoconfinement and channel guidance.
D7: clay-confined acid is reported to reduce leaching and improve immobilisation.
D4: confined phosphoric-acid or acid-complex environments are more likely to avoid disruptive crystallisation than neat water-rich phases.
D6: phosphoric acid supplies hydrogen-bond-mediated proton transfer within confined channels.

families.family_description: Amorphous phosphate-dominated phases provide continuous proton-relay landscapes with intrinsically retained acidic functionality.
descriptor_match: D1: protonated phosphate glass is explicitly amorphous and continuous for proton transport.
D4: phosphate-rich acid-complex or glassy environments keep the proton source in a non-crystalline form.
D6: phosphate groups provide strong hydrogen-bond donor/acceptor networks.
D7: protonated phosphate media intrinsically retain the conducting phase more strongly than free liquid acid.

instances.composition_description: A chitosan-PVA blended film using attapulgite as a 1-D confining filler and retained phosphoric acid as the proton-conducting phase.
expected_properties: cold_window: plausible bound-acid/water continuity in a hydrogen-bonded soft host
nanoconfinement: 1-D attapulgite may guide interconnected acid channels
retention: chitosan-clay interactions may suppress phosphoric-acid loss
risk_flags: PA leaching if acid loading is excessive
possible low-temperature stiffening without sufficient plasticisation
instances.novelty_rationale: The individual roles are supported, but this exact four-part composition is not directly claimed in the pool. It is a targeted cold-side analogue that swaps in retained PA for the proven chitosan/1-D-clay confinement motif.

instances.composition_description: A starch-PVA blend plasticised and protonated by a choline chloride/phosphoric acid deep eutectic acting as the retained conducting fraction.
expected_properties: cold_window: DES-like phase may resist freezing better than free water
proton_network: starch/PVA OH groups plus phosphate species support hybrid proton transfer
processability: blended polymer matrix should form continuous flexible films
risk_flags: excess DES may over-soften the membrane
acid-rich domains may still migrate under high humidity
instances.novelty_rationale: The DES acid-complex motif and the starch/PVA hydrogen-bonded host are separately supported, but their direct integration is not explicitly claimed. This combination is novel because it couples a cold-tolerant acid complex with an OH-rich biopolymer film-former pair.

instances.composition_description: A quaternary membrane combining starch host, PVA film former, halloysite nanotubes as 1-D confining filler, and phosphoric acid as the proton source.
expected_properties: cold_window: bound acid in an OH-rich matrix may maintain continuity below ambient
nanoconfinement: halloysite lumen/surface can localise acid and reduce channel disruption
synergy: starch-PVA compatibility may help disperse 1-D clay and preserve pathways
risk_flags: phosphoric-acid retention may depend strongly on clay loading
water management may still limit subzero conductivity
instances.novelty_rationale: This is the requested quaternary synergy pattern with support for each role but no exact pooled precedent. It is novel because it merges a starch/PVA biopolymer-film-former pair with a 1-D clay confinement route and retained PA conduction.

instances.composition_description: A chitosan film incorporating a proton-conducting deep eutectic solvent as the bound, plasticising acid phase.
expected_properties: cold_window: DES addition plausibly preserves mobile polar continuity toward 200 K
flexibility: DES should plasticise chitosan and reduce brittle low-temperature behaviour
retention: chitosan can hold high uptake without disintegration
risk_flags: exact DES chemistry may alter acidity and stability
instances.novelty_rationale: This exact match is retained as a control because the pool directly supports chitosan/DES blend films. It benchmarks the colder-window design logic against a literature-grounded plasticised biopolymer electrolyte.

instances.composition_description: An amorphous phosphate-glass host infiltrated with a choline chloride/phosphoric acid complex to couple retained phosphate sites with a non-crystallising acid medium.
expected_properties: pathway_continuity: amorphous phosphate host supports non-crystalline transport domains
acid_form: ChCl/PA complex may remain more mobile than neat phosphoric acid
retention: phosphate-rich host should suppress gross liquid loss
risk_flags: interfacial incompatibility between rigid glass and liquid complex
conditional long-term conductivity stability in phosphate glass
instances.novelty_rationale: No pooled claim gives this composite directly, but both the amorphous phosphate-retention motif and the ChCl/PA acid-complex motif are supported. The novelty lies in combining an intrinsically proton-active phosphate host with a cold-stable acid complex rather than relying on free hydrated acid alone.
